summary: Interpreting the recovery receipt 2cd3883705a64c35aa04ba14b815ea42, where all three comparisons are complete and satisfied: the member restarted with committed and applied index 2, then reported leader 1 and recovered the payload committed while it was down (parsed index 37: recovered true, commit and applied index 3, observed on all three nodes), a proposal from it returned with no error (index 38), and that proposal committed on all three nodes (index 39). The interpretation is recorded with conclusion holds and no defect judgment, plus a knowledge entry carrying the indices, and its rationale notes the structural contrast with the parent defect: a restarted member starts without a leader, so learning one arms its proposal gate, whereas the re-admitted member already believes a leader is known and therefore observes no leader change. Limits are stated explicitly: single restart, reliable delivery, no ticks during the outage, no snapshot installation and no storage loss, membership unchanged, and the clock advanced by the harness because the restarted member otherwise receives no leader traffic in this setup. Separately, a robustness variant of the primary scenario was prepared and verified locally under the recommended production configuration, PreVote and CheckQuorum, with the clock running: the witness invocation on the re-added member returned false at 901 ms with leader 1 still in StateLeader and the member a voter, its payload was not committed, while the never-removed member returned true and committed on all three nodes, so the held-proposal effect is not an artifact of default flags or of a clock that never advances. That variant is ready to be submitted next.
